newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya faces major power shortages in coming weeks.
newsitem.headline: Kenya faces major power shortages in coming weeks.

text.p: The repair of two generators at Kenya's main power station will force power rationing for about 13 weeks, authorities said on Monday.
The Kenya Power & Lighting Company Limited said work on the two machines with a capacity of 144 megawatts at Kiambere power station would start next Monday.
It said it would ration power to customers on a rotational basis from next Monday and work would take about 13 weeks.
KP&LC said in a statement the two machines were rated at 72 megawatts each but were operating at only 55 megawatts each because of a problem with insulation of the rotor poles.
"The two units will be taken out one at a time and after the repairs they will be operated at their full capacity of 72 megawatts each, boosting capacity by 34 megawatts," it added.
Kenya already has a power deficit of about 50 megawatts, said KP&LC. The system's peak demand was 670 megawatts while current available capacity was 620 megawatts.
"The absence of one unit at Kiambere will raise the capacity deficit to 105 megawatts," KP&LC said.
A KP&LC official declined to say how much the work would cost but KP&LC has been negotiating for financing of up to 1.2 billion shillings for a medium-term development programme.
Many large manufacturers and some households have bought generators for use during power cuts. A 75-megawatt thermal generating station, with funding by Japan, is unlikely to operate before 1999.

Kenya has tendered for three projects to raise the national capacity by about 105 megawatts in what is seen as a stop-gap measure. One company is to install a floating generator at the port of Mombasa by June 1997.
